comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a hydraulic shock absorber setting; pr-1444 safely sets a spring rat trap by restraining its hammer and latching its lock bar.
comparison.physical_skill: Both involve stored-energy mechanisms and bimanual stabilization. Candidate additionally requires recessed hex-key alignment, setscrew release and torque-limited locking, fine adjuster rotation, and response-guided iteration; pr-1444 requires continuously restraining a spring-loaded hammer while positioning a lock bar into a catch and avoiding the strike path.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable non-bottoming impact cycles, retained adjustment, no hard-stop strike, and safe de-energized manipulation. pr-1444 requires the hammer held at least 160 degrees back by a latched bar, no snap above 200 degrees/s, no unprotected gripper in the strike path, and both arms clear/home.
comparison.reason: The shared stored-energy hazard and bimanual holding are meaningful but do not make the tasks duplicates. The trap tests safe restraint and latching of a binary mechanism; the candidate tests calibrated dynamic absorption and setting retention across repeated cycles. Candidate still lacks numeric rebound, overload, collar-drift, witness-torque, locking-torque, and thread-damage thresholds.
